phase: The errand rule loses an arbitrary restriction: it now picks the citizen's largest out-of-home category instead of their largest of four service categories. Twenty-one of sixty then get a meal out, which is the denominator DS-1 has never had. The timing is disclosed - this was changed after learning DS-1 has no dine-in to collapse. What the round tests is the collapse rate, which the scenario does not set.
primary: Paired per-citizen composition distance against the v18 v25 arm, resampling citizens. Success is a 95% interval that excludes zero on the closer side. The same test on v34 gave -0.0198 [-0.0855, +0.0405], so a difference under about 0.06 cannot be told apart at this roster size.
limitations: The rule change was made after seeing that DS-1 lacks a denominator. The scenario now supplies dine-in; it does not decide how much of it survives the policy. Read every DS-1 number with that ordering in mind.
Twenty-seven of sixty get groceries, which the plans already used heavily, so the extra dine-in is the only real change for most of the cohort.
The errand stays optional. It can be deferred or dropped, and line 9 of the prompt says so.
preflight: 277 unit checks passed including 6 new resource-gate regressions. Source, v25 and asset_transaction_v7 unchanged from the previous round.
selection: Closed pair carried from v16/v17 (experiments/v18/prompt_v18.md). No new candidate.
